name: Turkey a la King over Egg Noodles
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Retro diner dish, no catalog equivalent (the creamy chicken-and-mushroom entry is a slow-cooker bowl, not a la king). Source verified at 4 servings, 438 cal / 11g protein but it is the chicken version; our turkey build loads the protein to ~540 cal / 35g. Confidence: source is chicken, not turkey; numbers are our build. | HARVEST: Source is Chicken a la King - uses cooked chicken, not turkey, and publishes no egg noodles in the ingredient list. Nutrition covers the a la King sauce only, excludes noodles.
OVERRIDE +Egg Noodles: WAVE-4: title base was MISSING - a la king OVER EGG NOODLES needs the noodles (62 g dry/serving x 4)
OVERRIDE Butter: WAVE-4 roux sanity: source 1/2 cup butter for 4 is restaurant-rich; house roux 1/3 cup
OVERRIDE Heavy Cream: WAVE-4: source is 1 cup HALF-AND-HALF; counted as its ~half cream fraction instead of a full cup of heavy cream
OVERRIDE Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast: TITLE-PROTEIN SWAP: titled turkey; diced chicken -> diced turkey breast, grams kept
intro_html: A la king was a fixture on American hotel menus for decades, then it fell out of fashion and everybody forgot how good it is. Turkey and mushrooms in a cream sauce, peas for color, olives for a salty little surprise, spooned over egg noodles. Each serving carries 40 grams of protein and 727 calories for about $2.64. Retro is only a criticism until you taste it.
ingredients_display: Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 30.75 oz dry (875 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Chicken Broth, 1.8 cartons: ~$2.26. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 32oz cartons.
Pantry seasonings (garlic powder, black pepper, salt): ~$0.32. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $36.96 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.64 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $55.42 across 14 servings, roughly $3.96 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $8.55 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $63.97. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.64 a serving. Mushrooms, cream, and butter push this one up the scale, and the payoff is a sauce that eats like something off a supper club menu.
shop_smart: White mushrooms in 8 oz packs cost roughly half what pre-sliced baby bellas do and there are eleven cups of them in this recipe. Slicing them yourself is the single biggest saving available here.
Heavy cream is the second cost driver. Buy pints rather than half pints, since the price per ounce drops sharply and cream freezes if you do not use it all.
Canned sliced olives in the 6 oz cans are far cheaper than anything from the olive bar and they are getting stirred into a cream sauce, where nobody can tell the difference.
Two frozen turkey breast roasts cover this batch. Cook both at once and freeze the extra diced meat for another dish.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Melt the butter in your largest pot over medium heat and cook the sliced mushrooms and diced onion for 10 to 12 minutes, until all the mushroom liquid has cooked away and they start to brown.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for two full minutes. This is a big roux and it needs the time to lose its raw taste.
Pour in the chicken broth gradually, whisking hard after each addition so no lumps form, and bring it to a simmer until it thickens.
Stir in the heavy cream and season with the garlic powder, salt, and plenty of black pepper, then let it bubble gently for 5 minutes.
Fold in the diced turkey breast and warm it through without boiling, since hard boiling will make the turkey tighten and go stringy.
Add the frozen peas and the sliced olives at the very end and let the residual heat warm them for 3 to 4 minutes, which keeps the peas bright instead of gray.
Cook egg noodles separately and spoon the a la king over them just before portioning, so the noodles do not swell and drink the sauce overnight.
portion_html: Weigh the pot of a la king, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Ladle that weight over each portion of noodles so the sauce, not the noodles, sets the serving size. Each serving comes to 727 calories and 40 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from spendwithpennies.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: A supper club classic for about $2.64 a serving, and this is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, for $1 a month.

head.description: Turkey a la king meal prep: turkey and mushrooms in a cream sauce with peas and olives, served over egg noodles. 727 calories, 40g protein, about $2.64 a serving.
head.keywords: turkey a la king, chicken a la king, creamy turkey and mushrooms, leftover turkey recipes, retro dinner, budget meal prep
steps: Cook the mushrooms and onion in butter 10 to 12 minutes until browned and dry.
Stir in the flour for two minutes, then whisk in the chicken broth and simmer until thickened.
Add the heavy cream and season with garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Fold in the diced turkey and warm through without boiling.
Stir in the peas and olives off the heat, spoon over cooked egg noodles, and portion into 14 containers.
